questions.q: A reader learned from the magazine a new way of looking at anger. What was it?
options: Anger must be expressed at once to stay healthy
Not quite. The article says: Anger releases great energy, and by staying silent in that moment it can be turned to positive use.
Anger releases great energy, and by staying silent in that moment it can be turned to positive use
Yes. She learned to direct it into positive channels.
Anger can be cured only by medicine
Not quite. The article says: Anger releases great energy, and by staying silent in that moment it can be turned to positive use.
Anger is a sign of strong character
Not quite. The article says: Anger releases great energy, and by staying silent in that moment it can be turned to positive use.
questions.rationale: “If you remain silent in a moment of anger, nature will take its own course and anger will be converted into positive energy.”

questions.q: “Live in this world as though you were a wayfarer.” How does this outlook help a person, according to the article?
options: He bears losses without bitterness and keeps his true destination in mind
Right. Even the urge for revenge is stilled.
He never settles in one town
Not quite. The article says: He bears losses without bitterness and keeps his true destination in mind.
He saves money for his travels
Not quite. The article says: He bears losses without bitterness and keeps his true destination in mind.
He avoids all responsibilities
Not quite. The article says: He bears losses without bitterness and keeps his true destination in mind.
questions.rationale: “It will enable him to bear all kinds of afflictions and losses without embitterment, as at any moment he may be on the brink of a new life.”

questions.q: “In the evening do not wait for the morning.” What does the saying urge?
options: Finish all work before sunset
Not quite. The article says: Use the present moment well; do not put off living rightly to a later time.
Stay awake through the night
Not quite. The article says: Use the present moment well; do not put off living rightly to a later time.
Do not make any plans
Not quite. The article says: Use the present moment well; do not put off living rightly to a later time.
Use the present moment well; do not put off living rightly to a later time
Well read. Each moment is too precious to waste on negativity.
questions.rationale: “Each moment of his life is precious—too precious to be squandered in negative thought or reaction.”

questions.q: From what discovery, the article says, is an introspective mind born?
options: The discovery of one’s hidden talents
Not quite. The article says: The discovery of one’s own helplessness – that one has no power over life, death or what sustains life.
The discovery of one’s own helplessness – that one has no power over life, death or what sustains life
Yes. That is the secret of purification.
The discovery of a wise teacher
Not quite. The article says: The discovery of one’s own helplessness – that one has no power over life, death or what sustains life.
The discovery of other people’s faults
Not quite. The article says: The discovery of one’s own helplessness – that one has no power over life, death or what sustains life.
questions.rationale: “An introspective mentality is born out of a discovery—that of one’s own helplessness.”

questions.q: How, according to the article, is a person purified?
options: Through his own struggle and repeated honest self-appraisal, led by conscience
Correct. Not by some mysterious inspiration from another.
Through the blessing of a saintly person
Not quite. The article says: Through his own struggle and repeated honest self-appraisal, led by conscience.
Through living apart from society
Not quite. The article says: Through his own struggle and repeated honest self-appraisal, led by conscience.
Through the passing of years
Not quite. The article says: Through his own struggle and repeated honest self-appraisal, led by conscience.
questions.rationale: “Purifying oneself involves struggle on the part of the individual. It is not at all related to any mysterious inspiration from some supposedly saintly person.”

questions.article: The Importance of a Secondary Role
questions.q: The article says a secondary role is not an inferior one. What special ability does the person who accepts it show?
options: Ego management
Right. For which the reward is double.
Readiness to stay silent always
Not quite. The article says: Ego management.
Skill in giving orders
Not quite. The article says: Ego management.
A lack of ambition
Not quite. The article says: Ego management.
questions.rationale: “Those who accept the secondary role will be rewarded doubly, because apart from their normal role, they have proved to have a great ability—ego management.”

questions.q: “Surely prayer restrains one from indecency and evil” (29:45). What test of true worship does the article draw from this?
options: Whether it is long and frequent
Not quite. The article says: Whether it shows in a person’s conduct – modesty and peace towards others.
Whether it is performed in a large gathering
Not quite. The article says: Whether it shows in a person’s conduct – modesty and peace towards others.
Whether others praise it
Not quite. The article says: Whether it shows in a person’s conduct – modesty and peace towards others.
Whether it shows in a person’s conduct – modesty and peace towards others
Well reasoned. Otherwise it is a spiritless ritual.
questions.rationale: “If one’s worship reflects in one’s behaviour, then it is worship in the true sense of the word.”

questions.article: Root Cause of Terrorism and Its Solution
questions.q: What example does the article take from the Prophet’s peace treaty at Hudaybiyah?
options: He agreed to the treaty for a single year
Not quite. The article says: He accepted the other side’s terms to secure peace, and peace opened the way to constructive work.
He left the matter to others to settle
Not quite. The article says: He accepted the other side’s terms to secure peace, and peace opened the way to constructive work.
He delayed the treaty until every right was granted
Not quite. The article says: He accepted the other side’s terms to secure peace, and peace opened the way to constructive work.
He accepted the other side’s terms to secure peace, and peace opened the way to constructive work
Yes. “Ignore the problems, and avail of the opportunities.”
questions.rationale: “In this treaty he unilaterally accepted all the conditions of his opponents… to enter into a 10-year no-war pact. This gave him and his Companions an opportunity to work uninterruptedly on a constructive programme.”

questions.q: The article contrasts two ways of living. What are they?
options: Merely passing time, and availing of time
Exactly. “A day you have lived fully was your day.”
Working and resting
Not quite. The article says: Merely passing time, and availing of time.
Earning and spending
Not quite. The article says: Merely passing time, and availing of time.
Speaking and listening
Not quite. The article says: Merely passing time, and availing of time.
questions.rationale: “There are two ways of leading life. One is to simply pass time, and the other is to avail of time.”

questions.q: In what sense does the article call the present world a “nursery”?
options: People grow and are tested here, and those who prove fit are chosen to be settled in Paradise
Well read. Freedom here is the test.
It is a place for children only
Not quite. The article says: People grow and are tested here, and those who prove fit are chosen to be settled in Paradise.
It is a garden meant for enjoyment
Not quite. The article says: People grow and are tested here, and those who prove fit are chosen to be settled in Paradise.
It is where life ends for good
Not quite. The article says: People grow and are tested here, and those who prove fit are chosen to be settled in Paradise.
questions.rationale: “Human beings grow in the nursery of this present world, and in the world of the Hereafter plants from this nursery are selected for being settled in Paradise.”
